title: Spectral hotspot mixer: synth workload + spectrometer for KV prefix cache p95 vs memory
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Objective: Build a synthetic workload generator (the 'hotspot mixer') plus a KV 'spectrometer' that decomposes prefix-cache hit-rate contributions by prefix-length, recency bucket, and token churn. Use the outputs to map tokens/sec and p95 tail latency as a function of memory footprint and workload mix.

Why: Existing harnesses measure overall hit-rate vs latency but lack fine-grained attribution and blended workload scenarios. In the wild, production traffic mixes stable long prefixes (high reuse) with short-lived ad-hoc prefixes and microbursts from feature experiments. We need a repeatable way to: 1) synthesize those mixes, 2) surface which prefix classes drive p95 and memory pressure, and 3) detect regressions in CI before releases.

Success criteria: 1) Hotspot mixer can produce configurable mixes (stable long-tail, exploratory short prefixes, bursty experiments) and stream at target tokens/sec up to 1M tokens/sec in dedicated cluster mode. 2) Spectrometer emits per-prefix-length hit-rate, per-recency-bucket hit-rate, per-shard occupancy, tokens/sec, and p95 latency histograms every 10s. 3) Dashboards and a regression detector alert if p95 regresses >10% or hit-rate drops >5% for top prefix bands. 4) CI integration: a benchmark job that runs on PRs to runtime and kvcache changes and fails when a threshold is exceeded.

Approach: Implement three components in the harness repo: (A) workload-synth service (Go) with config DSL for mixing strategy and token sequence generation; (B) spectrometer exporter (Rust) that attaches to kvcache telemetry hooks and computes attribution slices; (C) analysis runner (Python) that runs sweeps across memory budget and records tokens/sec vs p95 curves and creates canonical fingerprints for regression detection.

Measurement plan: Sweep memory budgets (e.g., 2GB, 4GB, 8GB, 16GB) and mixer mixes (stable:short:burst ratios of 80:15:5, 60:30:10, adversarial high-churn 30:65:5) and log: total tokens/sec, per-100ms p95, tail p99, hit-rate by prefix length (<64 tokens, 64-256, 256-1024, >1024), eviction churn, and per-shard occupancy. Store results in bench S3 bucket and produce time-series for Grafana.

Trade-offs and constraints: Emulating realistic token sequences requires stateful generators and KV warm-up time; to avoid flakiness we will maintain deterministic RNG seeds and capture warm-up windows separately. Running near 1M tokens/sec requires dedicated infra — will be run on dedicated capacity CI runners and cannot run on shared dev runners.

Artifacts: Confluence design doc (proto + DSL) and measurement templates, initial Grafana dashboard and Prometheus metrics schema.

acceptance_criteria: Hotspot mixer can run stable config and reproduce same hit-rate curve for 3 consecutive runs with seed fixed
Spectrometer emits per-prefix and per-recency metrics at 10s resolution and matches offline instrumentation within 2%
Benchmark sweep produces tokens/sec vs p95 curves for at least 3 memory budgets and stores results in bench S3
Regression detector job exists in CI; PRs changing kvcache runtime fail if p95 regresses >10% for a canonical profile
Runbook added for interpreting spectrometer slices and triaging top contributing prefix classes
